title: Proper locally acyclic morphisms have invertible higher-image specialization
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism], and $G$ a torsion abelian sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]; torsion means every local section is locally killed by a positive integer. Suppose $f$ is locally acyclic relative to $G$ [def-weil-pbc-local-acyclicity-abelian-sheaf]. Then for every integer $q\ge0$, every geometric point $\bar s$ of $S$, and every geometric point $\bar t$ of $S_{(\bar s)}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], the canonical specialization homomorphism
$$\operatorname{sp}:(R^qf_*G)_{\bar s}\longrightarrow(R^qf_*G)_{\bar t}$$
is an isomorphism of abelian groups. Here the target stalk is at the composite geometric point of $S$, higher direct images are computed in abelian sheaves as in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], stalks are those of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], and specialization is the homomorphism obtained by restricting pointed etale neighbourhood germs through $S_{(\bar s)}\to S$. No smoothness or local constancy of $G$ is assumed, nor any finiteness of its stalks.

source.place: Tag 0GJW, lemma-sp-isom-proper-torsion-loc-ac, specialization for K=G[0] and degree-q cohomology

proof.text: Form the strict-local base change f prime and its two fibre inclusions. Properness and the qcqs conditions are inferred from the existing Mathlib permanence instances. The strict-local ring is strictly henselian by strictHenselizationLocalStructure. Canonical evaluation factors through its surjective map to the relative separable closure; the surjection is local, and its inclusion into the geometric-point field is local. Thus canonical evaluation is a local homomorphism. The residue field of an algebraically closed field is algebraically closed by the bijective residue homomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0GJW, proof specialized to G[0]; step 1

proof.text: A torsion sheaf G placed in degree zero has torsion homology: H^0 is G and all other homology objects are zero. For any proper geometric fibre square, proper base change makes derived exchange invertible. The definition etaleDerivedFiberMap is inverse geometric-point stalk comparison, stalk of this exchange, and inverse derived global germ; all are invertible. Paste the two pullback squares and compose with the inverse-image composition and single-functor comparison to obtain invertibility of strictBaseSheafFiberMap. The closed fibre map additionally contains only an equality transport, hence is invertible too.

source.place: Tag 0GJW, proof specialized to G[0]; step 2

proof.text: Inverse image preserves torsion by the existing isTorsion_upperStar theorem. Apply qcqs_higherDirectImages_prime_torsion to h and the pulled-back sheaf with the set of all primes. The torsion-sheaf characterization using algebraically closed geometric points turns its elementwise positive annihilators into the torsion condition on every nonnegative homology sheaf. Negative homology vanishes by preservation of the lower cohomological bound under right derivation. Transport along the exact-inverse-image single-functor comparison. This proves torsion homology for K prime = Rh_*h^{-1}G prime[0]. Local acyclicity makes the closed-fibre inverse image of the derived unit invertible.

source.place: Tag 0GJW, proof specialized to G[0]; step 3

proof.text: For any proper cartesian square over a local map of strictly henselian rings and any bounded-below torsion complex K, proper base change makes exchange invertible. In each integer degree the strict-local derived-global-exchange theorem gives additive equivalences c1,c2 and c2 e = p c1. Since e and the equivalences are bijective, the homology of derived restriction p is bijective. The homology criterion in D plus makes restriction itself invertible. Apply this to canonical evaluation and K prime from step 3. Expand etaleCospecialization: inverse Leray, this invertible restriction, and derived global sections of the inverse closed-fibre unit. Consequently cospecialization is invertible.

source.place: Tag 0GJW, proof specialized to G[0]; step 4

proof.text: Specialization-cospecialization compatibility gives sp followed by the other fibre map and cospecialization equal to the closed fibre map. Cancel the invertible other factors to prove derived specialization invertible. Its definition conjugates the derived natural transformation induced by underived specialization by exact-functor comparisons, so that derived natural transformation is invertible at Rf_*G[0]. To pass to degree q, choose a bounded-below complex representative. The natural-transformation derived-unit equation and invertibility of the units for exact stalk functors make the termwise transformation a quasi-isomorphism at this representative. The homology comparison with localization and NatTrans.app_homology identify its degree-q homology with the underived transformation evaluated on H^q. Isomorphism invariance transports this along the representative comparison. This is exactly the displayed etaleStalkSpecialization.

split_report.summary: Audited the imported five-step Tag 0GJW specialization proof against every cited DAG statement. The construction of the strict henselian base, proper/qcqs hypotheses, fibre comparison, torsion preservation, exchange/restriction identification, and final degree-q passage are all retained; no new child node is needed. The 2138-character exchange-identification step was checked as one routine representative-level map calculation, with its termwise exchange and derived pullback definitions cited explicitly. Maintainer reader (2026-10-17): step 4's inline representative-level identification of the closed-fibre exchange with restriction duplicated the existing reviewed node lem-weil-pbc-strict-local-derived-global-exchange (unit sk-thm-p1, on the route); step 4 now cites it together with thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below, and the five nodes used only by the inline calculation were dropped from proof_deps.
split_report.blueprint: Proof, first paragraph: "the sheaves $R^qf_{\Et,*}F_{\Et}$ are constructible and zero for $q>2e$". Constructibility clause, via the existing 0GL0 -> 0GKW -> 0GKV case (a) -> 0GKD branch; 0GKD invokes 0GJQ, 0GJR and 0GJW.

tool_uses.why: Step 1 uses clause (1) to obtain the strictly henselian local base and the canonical closed geometric lift; this is a generic strict-henselization fact, not a replacement for the proper-base-change argument.
Steps 2 and 4 use the natural Leray identification and the derived-unit formula identifying cohomology pullback along i; these are generic adjunction tools, not another proof route.
Step 3 uses the inverse-image stalk isomorphism to preserve elementwise torsion under pullback; this is a generic stalk calculation.

Step 3 applies the existing qcqs higher-image theorem with the set of all primes to the affine h; the unit has no torsion-preservation statement for arbitrary qcqs maps. It supplies precisely the input 0DDD used in the source proof and does not replace any step of the unit route.
